# Pulse task #2748: Plan signed direct-distribution Hex updates with deferred installation

Operation: 3abd43b24503c4e0ddbc53640651cf81
Assignee: PORTALSURFER (Pulse #1, GitHub ID 41680373)

PLANNING ONLY — future direct-distribution update design, not implementation/release authorization. Keep todo. Do not create keys/certificates, publish an appcast, deploy servers, submit notarization, install frameworks or change the running app from this planning task.

Distribution choice
Recommend direct Developer ID distribution if an in-app updater is desired. A Mac App Store edition must instead use store-delivered updates and omit its own updater, per Apple guideline2.4.5(vii). Local development is a separate mode: no Apple notarization submission for each local iteration. Shipping-channel choice can wait; it does not block local staging #2746.

Existing versus new
Existing: exact optimized source/CI and artifact receipts, stable app target/bundle identity, serialized checked replacement, temporary publication custody, fast ./launch. Installed253003639 is still ad-hoc/unsigned-bundle packaging; Developer ID/notarized distribution, signed feeds, downloader, updater framework, automatic staging and safe save/restart are NOT current capabilities. #2745/PR355 owns stable signing and recurring Documents-folder permission diagnosis. Preserve that scope and source history.

Recommended implementation direction, subject to future authorization
1. Evaluate and pin a reviewed Sparkle2 release rather than implement a bespoke network updater/delta engine. Its official API supports downloaded updates installed on quit, but GPUI/Rust integration is not present. Record the native framework/helper/bridge boundary, license and provenance; keep GPUI, safe workspace code, crate responsibilities and real-time audio boundaries. Do not switch UI frameworks or adopt an unreviewed Rust wrapper implicitly. Shipping helpers must be correctly signed; do not disable production library validation to make a framework load.
2. Obtain source CI and optimized artifact first, then finalized Developer ID signing/hardened-runtime/required entitlements, notarization and ticket stapling for the public artifact, and final archive authentication. Reuse #2745’s verified identity contract once delivered. Any future update-signing keys/operator credentials and publication destination require explicit separate authorization; no new account, purchase or server is implied. Stable approved team/designated requirement, app ID and installation location must persist across ordinary updates. No silent migration from the user’s current org.portalsurfer.hex.dev or stable development path.
3. Authenticate remote metadata/artifacts, not just compare hashes. Use HTTPS, authenticated Sparkle update archives, trusted embedded update public key, compatible Developer ID identity and OS trust/notarization verification. Assess signed feed/notes and verification before extraction against the pinned version. Reject mismatched identity, invalid/untrusted archive, unsupported OS/architecture, stale candidate and prohibited downgrade before touching the app. Offer manual checks by default; scheduling/background download requires user preference. No signing secrets on the hosting endpoint or in Git/logs.
4. Replace hash-derived CFBundleVersion for shipping update ordering. Current installer uses int(source[:8],16), which is NOT monotonic. Define an increasing release build sequence and channel/version ordering, retaining the full Git source separately in HexSourceRevision/receipts. Prevent a random hash comparison from hiding updates or causing an unintended downgrade. Do not conflate local source selection with public release order.
5. Reuse #2746’s user contract: stage without restarting; install on the next approved normal quit (zero extra restarts), or one explicit save-and-restart after successful durable save. Preserve the canonical close/recording/pending-work rules and wait for actual process quiescence. Sparkle’s willInstallUpdateOnQuit hook is not a universal save/cancellation veto; its docs say it attempts installation when the app terminates. Prove the configured framework/arming lifecycle honors safe-close approval, including crash and cancellation, instead of assuming a callback protects unsaved documents. Do not force quit, replace a running binary, silently discard work or relaunch after ordinary quit without an explicit restart request. No live binary patching or OS reboot.
6. Keep installed app and settings/projects/media usable on download/signing/apply failure; retain authenticated pending state for truthful retry and use documented installer cleanup. No new routine revision-named review apps or permanent rollback copies. Evaluate framework temporary custody/cleanup against existing #2627 policy; do not silently relax it. An unwritable/read-only/translocated install must yield actionable guidance, not automatic chmod/root services or security-setting changes.
7. Actual OS folder access and Dock behavior must be measured across successive compatible signed updates with #2745’s owner. Stable path/ID alone is not proof of unchanged TCC permission or bookmark validity. No TCC reset, Full Disk Access workaround, permission grant bypass or duplicate folder-access investigation. A one-time trust transition from the present ad-hoc build may still need ordinary user consent.

Finite acceptance before release
- Approved channel/identity/path and pinned updater/bridge architecture; all signing/hosting/operator capabilities explicitly established rather than assumed.
- Two sequential increasing-version signed/notarized candidates update through a test feed at the same app target; authenticate the actual downloaded/extracted/installed artifact, source/release mapping and launched version.
- Corrupt archive, forged metadata/signature, wrong signer, incompatible build, stale/downgrade, offline check, canceled save, active recording, crash, concurrent installer and unwritable target preserve user work and report real state.
- At most one requested quit/relaunch for immediate activation; deferred mode has no additional forced restart; no automatic retry/relaunch loop.
- Real native save/cancel/reopen, Dock continuity and folder-grant retention evidence, plus exact local-only CI and platform scope recorded. No hosted/paid CI or claimed notarization until actual successful submissions/readback.

Dependencies / open decisions
Advisory dependencies #2746 (staging/clean quit contracts) and #2745/PR355 (stable signing/permissions). Reuse existing local transaction concept, not its source-worktree Python runtime as a shipping-app dependency.
Consequential later choice: direct distribution with an in-app updater versus Mac App Store with store-only updates; decide before shipping integration. Public channel, signing-key custody, approved feed/artifact destination and increasing build-number policy need explicit product/operator decisions before release. No such infrastructure or key work is authorized now.

Primary sources reviewed17October2026
Apple store update rule: https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/#hardware-compatibility
Developer ID and notarization: https://developer.apple.com/developer-id/ ; https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/notarizing-macos-software-before-distribution
Code identity across updates: https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/technotes/tn2206/_index.html
Sparkle setup/authentication/version ordering: https://sparkle-project.org/documentation/
Install-on-quit lifecycle API: https://sparkle-project.org/documentation/api-reference/Protocols/SPUUpdaterDelegate.html
Repository baseline: scripts/hex-test-build.py and docs/test-builds.md at f81a33f993b588faf9aa3a747cf6b1006e3c249f. No runtime/source changes made by this plan.
